ut_buckhorn_wash.blurb: A long, deep canyon in the San Rafael Swell of south-central Utah, far less famous than Moab or Indian Creek. All of the rock is sandstone, and because the canyon cuts through many layers several formations are climbed, including plenty of Wingate cracks. Trad dominates, with sport lines now appearing on featured faces, plus towers, a few aid routes and a good set of boulder problems. Grades are centred on 5.9 to 5.11, with a few harder and some easier. The wash is split at a petroglyph panel into Lower Buckhorn, the larger half, and Upper Buckhorn up-canyon.

wa_sub_wapass.blurb: Granite spires and towers along the North Cascades Highway, reached by driving north from Twisp through Mazama. The rock belongs to the Golden Horn batholith, and the highway keeps approaches short. Alpine trad is the core, with a smaller set of sport crags and a few scrambles, snow routes and ice lines. Grades span 5.4 up to 5.13, with the bulk from 5.8 to 5.12. Liberty Bell Group is the biggest cluster, with Silver Star and the Wine Spires, Hairpin Crags and Kangaroo Ridge also large. The best window runs from late June through September, and snow and ice can linger early in the season.

wy_blair_overview.blurb: A forested crag area at about 8,300 feet in Vedauwoo, southeast Wyoming, away from the busier central formations. Vedauwoo's rock is Sherman granite, and Blair is a crack venue: finger cracks through offwidths, with trad the dominant style plus some sport, top-rope and boulder problems. Grades run from easy fifth class to the 5.12s, with most between 5.9 and 5.12. Lower Blair holds Blair I, II and III and neighbouring formations, while Upper Blair sits about 200 feet higher, in a tight band of rocks where many routes face north and stay shaded for much of the day.

ca_jumbo_rock_area.blurb: A cluster of formations in the Pinto Basin side of Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,400 feet along Sheep Pass Road. The monzogranite is notably coarse and rough, with Conan's Corridor and Zebra Cliffs the better-textured exceptions. Trad dominates, with a smaller set of sport lines, some top-rope and a little bouldering. Grades are centred on 5.8 to 5.10, with a few at 5.11. Sun varies by wall: the southeast-facing Cunning Rock face catches the morning and works on cold days, and The Wedge is sheltered from north wind and warm in the sun. Other sizeable crags include Hen House and Dr. Haney's Tool Shed Area.

ca_p_cathedral_area.blurb: The Cathedral Rocks on the south side of Yosemite Valley, directly across from El Capitan: Lower, Middle and Higher Cathedral Rock, with two free-standing Cathedral Spires just east of the highest. The rock is granite, steep and smooth. Middle Cathedral is the main draw, known for long, sustained free routes, mostly trad and multi-pitch with some sport, top-rope and aid. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.13, most between 5.9 and 5.12. Bouldering adds problems from V0 to V7.
